key_insight: Fit-LRP tightens neural network verification bounds by optimizing affine relaxations over exact unions of polytopes instead of enclosing axis-aligned boxes.
engineering_relevance: This enables more efficient verification of cyber-physical systems with oblique or non-convex safety regions, including obstacle-avoidance and neural Lyapunov constraints.
method: Represent non-convex verification domains as unions of polytopes.
Optimize affine bounds over these domains using small, low-dimensional linear programs.
Integrate into LiRPA and α,β-CROWN branch-and-bound to enable earlier pruning.
evidence_signal: On ARCH-COMP and neural Lyapunov benchmarks, the abstract reports 47× less branching on the hardest region, 15× lower worst-case verification time, and, with region-wise partitioning, verification on a single CPU 6.1× faster than α,β-CROWN on a GPU.
watch_item: Exactness applies to optimizing the affine bounds, not the nonlinear network; scalability with polytope count and dimension remains an implementation concern.
paper_title: Fit-LRP: Fitting Linear Relaxations to Polytopes for Neural Network Verification over Non-Convex Regions
